study_identification_part.si4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with FirstEpisode Psychosis Using Normative Models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize 10-year longitudinal trajectories of cortical thickness deviations in first-episode psychosis and test their associations with symptoms using normative models.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear mixed-effects models tested main and interaction effects of diagnosis and time on deviation scores; additional LME assessed associations between deviations and PANSS total/general/negative scores while controlling for age and sex; supplementary t-tests and χ² tests compared groups and sex distributions; multiple comparisons controlled with BH-FDR.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Cortical thickness deviations in patients are more negative at baseline and attenuate over 10 years alongside symptom reductions; specific frontal/insular/ACC regions show associations with PANSS scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Significant conditional main effects of diagnosis and time × diagnosis interactions are observed across bilateral lateral temporal, parietal, and frontal regions and along medial frontal/parietal lobes. Deviations are more negative in patients at baseline and reduce over time with fewer significant differences at 12 months and none at 10 years. Median CT deviation effect sizes: baseline d = -0.46, 12-month d = -0.43, 10-year d = -0.27. LME reveals effects of anterior cingulate on PANSS total and insular/orbitofrontal regions on PANSS negative scores; raw CT shows aging/scanner confounds whereas normative deviations do not.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Reference HBR models trained across 77 sites were adapted via transfer learning to new scanners using local controls, effectively removing age/scanner effects in deviations; extreme deviation threshold |z| > 2 used; demonstrates feasibility of tracking longitudinal clinical trajectories using normative models.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Potential selection/retention biases; limited power to compare first- vs second-generation antipsychotics; extreme deviations may reflect confounds (noise, artifacts, comorbidities, medications); moderate sample size at 10-year follow-up; scanner changes across waves may influence findings despite validated framework.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Dataset names for the reference normative cohort were not listed; authors describe 'mostly publicly available datasets' across 77 sites. MRI scanners for TOP included 1.5T Siemens Magnetom Sonata, 3T GE Signa HDxT, and 3T GE Discovery 750 with acquisition details (see main text and Supplementary 'MRI scanners').
